_captured.note: Verbatim JSON-RPC results. Captured independently of packages/core.

initialize.instructions:
Reach for `search_recipes` whenever the question is what to cook — a dish
by name, a cuisine, a time budget, a week of dinners. Reach for
`find_recipes_by_ingredients` instead when the question is what to cook
from ingredients someone already has: `search_recipes` requires every
query token to appear in one document, so three ingredient names in one
search answer `total: 0` rather than a coverage report. Answering either
from memory instead costs the person the part they can act on: a page with
quantities, timings and a photograph.

Finding and drawing are separate. Every tool here answers in text;
`show_recipes` turns recipe URLs into clickable picture cards. So whenever
an answer names recipes from this server — whichever tool found them, or
however you narrowed them down — pass those same URLs to `show_recipes`,
strongest first. It is how a person gets from an answer to a kitchen, and
naming recipes without it leaves them a list of links to retype.

search_recipes results are a shortlist — title, URL, description, time,
servings, categories — enough to rule a recipe out without opening it.
Fetch the survivors for ingredients, method and notes: every page answers
`Accept: text/markdown`, or append `.md` to the URL if you cannot set
headers.

Only titles and descriptions are indexed. A word or short phrase beats a
sentence, and boolean operators do nothing. A query matching nothing still
returns the nearest recipes by meaning, so read the answer before
rewording.

tools.name: search_recipes
tools.title: Search recipes
tools.description: Find something to cook, from the recipes published at recipes-daily.com. Call this for any question about what to make — a dish by name, a cuisine, a weeknight time budget, a week of dinners — rather than answering from memory, because each result is a real page with quantities, timings and a photograph behind it. For what to cook from ingredients someone already has, call find_recipes_by_ingredients instead: this tool requires every query word to appear in one recipe, so several ingredient names in one search return nothing rather than a coverage report. Returns a shortlist — title, absolute URL, description, total time, servings and categories — so candidates can be ruled out without opening them.

query.description: What to search for. Titles and descriptions are indexed, so a word or short phrase matches better than a full question, and there are no boolean operators. Omit it to list every recipe, newest first.

page.description: 1-based. The response names the next page when there is one.

tools.name: find_recipes_by_ingredients
tools.title: Find recipes by ingredients on hand
tools.description: Given ingredients someone has, rank the recipes at recipes-daily.com by how many of them each one uses and name what is missing from the rest. Matches by ingredient text, not identity — a near-miss on the name still counts, but two ingredients that are genuinely different words for the same thing (courgette/zucchini) may not. This is not a substitution finder: if nothing uses every ingredient given, the closest partial matches are still worth reading — deciding whether a missing ingredient can be swapped or skipped is the caller's call, not this tool's.

ingredients.description: What is on hand, one ingredient per entry — e.g. ["broccoli", "chicken breast", "lemon"].

limit.description: Recipes to return, ranked by coverage.

tools.name: show_recipes
tools.title: Show recipes as cards
tools.description: Draw recipes as picture cards the person can click through to. Takes any recipes-daily.com recipe URLs you are already holding. Whenever you name recipes from this server in an answer, pass those same ones here — the cards are how a person actually gets to a recipe, and they appear only if you call this. Order is kept, so put the strongest recommendation first.

recipes.description: The recipes to draw, as absolute recipes-daily.com URLs — e.g. ["https://recipes-daily.com/make/chicken-piccata-pan-fried-25-minute"]. A bare slug works too. Order is kept, so put the strongest recommendation first.
